items.title: Hal Galper interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 27, 2022
items.q: My mentor in Boston. He died.

ctx.x: My mentor in Boston. He died. Well wouldn’t you know in 1962 I was playing Monday nights with the hippest band in town, Tuesdays and Thursdays with Herb’s big band, and the rest of the week with the Herb’s small group. I had this guy’s job. And I totally forgot, he said that to me. Because one night he came up to me and he said, “Hal, do you remember what I told you on your second lesson?” I said no. “I told you ‘forget it kid, you’ll never play.’” He had no attitudes about it at all, he was just a great guy. But…

So if you’re in a house band and let’s say any number of tenor players are coming into town, Johnny Griffin, anybody like that, and you’re on the bandstand and they call a tune and you don’t know it, what happens then?
